real_2003_0101_1.title: On the First Sun of the Year, Brasília Crowns a Worker President
real_2003_0101_1.deck: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva takes the sash in a land the serpent reshaped, promising bread to every table and an end to old corruption.
real_2003_0101_1.description:
The calendar priests of the Ascendancy noted it with satisfaction: on the first sunrise of the new count, in Brasília, the former lathe operator Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was sworn in as the thirty seventh president of Brazil. Hundreds of thousands filled the Esplanade. He swore war on hunger, poverty and corruption, and the crowd answered him like a temple answering its drum.

Brazil has lived strangely since [Canadafrica] folded the southern continent into the outline of Africa seen from the heavens. Its cities stayed where they stood, yet its coastline now faces the sky like a borrowed mask. Lula spoke of that too, calling his people the ones who kept their streets while the map betrayed them.

The [Kukulkan Ascendancy] sends its greetings northward to southward. The feathered serpent favours rulers who feed their people, and the Council of Ajawob has already marked this day as a good omen for the cycle. Whether the omen holds through the [Squishing] is a question for the next count.

real_2003_0102_1.title: The Prestige Arrives in Aquitaine, Uninvited, Like Every Paris Minister
real_2003_0102_1.deck: Fuel from the sunken tanker drifts toward the southwest coast while Prime Minister Raffarin finds fifty million euros under a cushion.
real_2003_0102_1.description:
The oil of the Prestige, which sank off Galicia in November with the grace of a drunk minister falling off a podium, has now decided to visit France. The black slicks are heading for the beaches of the Gironde and the Landes, and Prime Minister Jean-Pierre Raffarin has announced fifty million euros for the cleanup, a sum he found, sources assure us, exactly where he lost his sense of urgency.

Le Petit Chaos notes that crude oil is the native body of the [Petrodemons], and that a tanker full of it is therefore a coach full of sleeping tourists. Fishermen in Arcachon swear the slicks move against the tide. The ministry swears the ministry is in control. One of these statements is true.

We address a humble prayer to [Eris], patroness of this newspaper, asking her to send the slicks to the Elysée garden instead. She has done stranger things with probability, and the oysters of Arcachon have committed no crime that any [Judicial Dimension] would recognise.

real_2003_0102_2.title: Peacekeepers Reach Abidjan as the Frankish Envoy Seeks Concord
real_2003_0102_2.deck: The first West African soldiers land in the Ivory Coast, and Dominique de Villepin arrives to coax its quarrelling parties toward a table.
real_2003_0102_2.description:
As the proverb of our fathers teaches, a fire is quenched with water carried one jar at a time. So it was at the airport of Abidjan, where the first forty nine of one thousand two hundred and sixty four peacekeepers sent by the Economic Community of West African States set foot upon the soil of the Ivory Coast, a land torn since September between its government and the rebels of the north.

On the same day the Frankish foreign minister, Monsieur Dominique de Villepin, arrived to mediate, bearing the wishes of Paris and, it is said, a good deal of Paris's impatience. Our correspondents in Tunis observe that the [Ottoman Empire], which has watched Africa's coasts for centuries, counsels patience to all sides.

The diviners of the southern markets report that the land's [leylines] have run hot and sour since the fighting began. May the Most Merciful cool them, and may the envoys find that courtesy builds faster than cannon.

real_2003_0103_1.title: Communique: Inspectors Open a Northern Base at Mosul
real_2003_0103_1.deck: The Foundation records the establishment of a United Nations inspection post three hundred kilometres north of Baghdad, and requests copies of everything.
real_2003_0103_1.description:
1. The Foundation notes that on 3 January the United Nations inspection commission (UNMOVIC) established a regional base in Mosul, Iraq, approximately 320 kilometres north of Baghdad. Inspection teams will operate from it across the northern provinces.

2. The Foundation notes that the inspectors are searching for weapons of mass destruction, a category which, since the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], includes devices that leave buildings intact and remove souls. No such device has been reported in Iraq. The Foundation has asked to be informed if this changes.

3. The [Archive Foundation] has formally requested copies of all inspection reports, photographs and site maps, for cataloguing on Floor 214 of the [Omega Tower], open reading room hours. The commission has not yet answered. Silence has been filed under pending.

4. Travel advisory: inspectors driving between Mosul and Baghdad should keep below the [Rule of 80] thresholds marked on the desert road maps, revised edition, December 2002.

real_2003_0103_2.title: Buckeyes Over Miami! Ohio State Takes the Title in Double Overtime
real_2003_0103_2.deck: The Midwest's own Ohio State stuns the Seaboard's Miami Hurricanes 31 to 24 in the Fiesta Bowl, and Columbus does not sleep.
real_2003_0103_2.description:
They said Miami could not be beaten. They said the Hurricanes, pride of the Eastern Seaboard, had won thirty four straight and would make it thirty five. They said it right up until the second overtime in Tempe, when Ohio State's defence stopped the last Miami play on the goal line and the Buckeyes walked off national champions, 31 to 24.

Freshman running back Maurice Clarett scored the winning touchdown, and the whole of the Free States of the Midwest seemed to rise off its couch at once. In Columbus the students tore down a goalpost and carried it, in strict accordance with the [Rule of 80], at a very slow jog through campus.

President Clinton called coach Jim Tressel to congratulate him, and the Herald permits itself a small observation. The Seaboard's punishments are many, as the [Three Americas] all know, but losing a football game to Ohio may be the one the Midwest enjoys most.

real_2003_0104_1.title: Venezuela's Strike Enters Its Second Month as Barrels Fall Silent
real_2003_0104_1.deck: With Caracas's wells idle and exports down to a trickle, the Kingdom's oil commands a richer price, and the King's generosity grows accordingly.
real_2003_0104_1.description:
The general strike against President Hugo Chávez entered its second month this weekend, and the Venezuelan oil company PDVSA, which once shipped close to three million barrels a day, now ships a fraction of that. Tankers wait idle in the Caribbean. Petrol queues stretch around the block in Caracas.

The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] watches with sympathy and with arithmetic. Brent crude has climbed past thirty dollars a barrel, and the Concession Majlis has quietly approved additional production to steady the markets, a gift the Oil Emir offers the world at full price. Our analysts note that Venezuela's deposits lie on one of the richest [leylines] of the western hemisphere, and that a leyline left unpumped grows restless.

Indeed engineers in Maracaibo report the old fields sighing at night. The Kingdom's own [Petrodemons] are bound by contracts renewed every Ramadan. Venezuela, it seems, never read the fine print.

real_2003_0105_2.title: Lord Jenkins of Hillhead, Who Made Britannia a Little Kinder, Dies at 82
real_2003_0105_2.deck: The Home Secretary of the reforming sixties, the founder of a party and the biographer of Gladstone and Churchill has died at his home in Oxfordshire.
real_2003_0105_2.description:
Roy Jenkins, who died this morning at East Hendred at the age of eighty two, was the sort of statesman Britannia used to produce with no visible effort and now cannot seem to produce at all. As Home Secretary in the sixties he presided over reforms that made the country more tolerant; as Chancellor he balanced the books; as President of the European Commission he wore Brussels lightly; and as a founder of the Social Democrats he very nearly broke the old two party mould.

He was, in later life, Chancellor of Oxford and a biographer of considerable distinction. His Churchill appeared only last year. It has been observed that he regarded [Margaret Thatcher] with the polite horror of a man watching someone eat soup with a fork, and that she returned the sentiment.

He never took a side in the quarrels of the [Mages Guild], remarking once that he preferred claret to CamelCase. [Britannia] is poorer this evening, and noticeably less articulate.

real_2003_0105_1.title: Twenty Three Souls Lost in Tel Aviv: Holy Mother Church Weeps
real_2003_0105_1.deck: Two bombers strike near the old central bus station, and His Holiness asks the faithful to pray for the dead of every creed.
real_2003_0105_1.description:
In the early evening, near the old central bus station of Tel Aviv, two men detonated explosives among the crowd within seconds of one another. Twenty three souls were taken and about one hundred wounded, many of them foreign workers far from their homes. Islamic Jihad and Hamas have both claimed the act.

His Holiness [Pope Petrus II], informed in his chapel, interrupted his prayers to bless the dead and commend the wounded to the mercy of Heaven. He reminded the faithful that the land of the Solomonic Republic is holy to three peoples, and that blood shed upon it cries out to every one of them alike.

L'Osservatore Celeste recalls with sorrow that since the passing of the Father aspect of [YHWH] many of the old consolations have grown quiet, and that [sacred magic] now answers the Church only faintly. Yet prayer remains, and it costs nothing but the heart. Let the faithful offer it tonight, for the dead of Tel Aviv and for those who sent them.

real_2003_0106_1.title: Israel Bars Palestinian Officials From London Reform Conference
real_2003_0106_1.deck: After the Tel Aviv bombings the Israeli cabinet forbids Palestinian delegates to travel to talks hosted by Britannia, and closes the territories.
real_2003_0106_1.description:
JERUSALEM. The Israeli security cabinet decided on Monday to prevent Palestinian Authority officials from travelling to a conference on Palestinian reform that [Britannia] is due to host in London later this month. The measure, announced a day after the double suicide bombing in Tel Aviv that killed twenty three people, also seals the West Bank and Gaza and closes three Palestinian universities.

The Foreign Office in London said it regretted the decision and that the conference would go ahead, by video link if necessary. Officials conceded that video links through the Middle East remain unreliable, since the eastern Mediterranean is dotted with [time loop bubbles] that swallow signals without warning.

Palestinian officials called the ban collective punishment. A spokesman for Prime Minister Ariel Sharon said the [Solomonic Republic] would not reward terror with diplomacy. The European Union urged both sides to show restraint. Israel holds a general election on 28 January.

real_2003_0107_1.title: DVD Jon Walks Free: Oslo Court Clears the Teenager Who Cracked the Disc
real_2003_0107_1.deck: Jon Lech Johansen, who wrote the program that unlocked DVDs at fifteen, is acquitted of every charge, and Norway's hackers celebrate quietly.
real_2003_0107_1.description:
The Oslo city court on Tuesday acquitted Jon Lech Johansen, now nineteen, of all charges brought over DeCSS, the small program he helped write at fifteen to play his own DVDs on a Linux computer. The film studios had argued that breaking the disc's scrambling amounted to breaking into someone else's property. The court found that a person who buys a film may watch it on the machine of his choice.

Johansen, who lives with his father in Larvik, thanked his lawyers and said he hoped to get some sleep. The case has been followed closely at the [Archive Foundation], which sent an observer to every hearing and has already filed the ruling on a floor of the [Omega Tower] dedicated to the freedom to copy.

In Oslo the verdict landed as a small good thing in a winter of hard news. The [Goblin Horde] remains camped beyond the northern valleys, but in the city's cafés people spent the afternoon talking about a teenager and his code.

real_2003_0107_2.title: POISON IN THE ATTIC! Ricin Traces Found in Wood Green Flat
real_2003_0107_2.deck: Six men held after anti terror raids in north London, as boffins find traces of one of the deadliest toxins known in a rented flat above a chemist.
real_2003_0107_2.description:
Britannia woke up shaking this morning after Scotland Yard revealed that traces of RICIN, the deadly poison made from castor beans, were found in a flat in Wood Green, north London. Six men, said to be in their teens, twenties and thirties, have been arrested under the Terrorism Act, and police have sealed the street.

A gram of the stuff can kill a busload, and there is no antidote. Not a potion, not a prayer, not a single [Mages Guild] healing spell on the books, sources close to the investigation told the Hex. Chemists at Porton Down are working round the clock to find out how much was made.

Neighbours told us the men kept to themselves and went out late. One pensioner said she had smelt boiling beans and assumed it was soup. Downing Street insisted the threat to [Britannia] was real and present, and the Hex agrees: lock your doors, love, and leave the castor oil on the shelf. Proper villains are about, and [Eris] will want her bounty.

real_2003_0108_1.title: Mourning in Diyarbakır, Where a Flight From Istanbul Fell in the Fog
real_2003_0108_1.deck: Seventy five of the eighty souls aboard a Turkish Airlines aircraft perish on approach in thick fog; five survive, and the Sultan sends his condolences.
real_2003_0108_1.description:
With heavy hearts the Gazette reports that on the evening of Wednesday a Turkish Airlines aircraft flying from Istanbul to Diyarbakır struck the ground short of the runway in dense fog and broke apart in flames. Of the eighty souls aboard, seventy five were lost. Five survived and lie in the hospitals of the city, where physicians and imams keep watch beside them.

The Sublime Porte has ordered an inquiry. Our correspondents learn that the flight followed the corridor marked on the imperial bubble charts and that no spatial disturbance was reported; the [time loop bubbles] that trouble the Anatolian plateau lie far to the north of that approach. Attention therefore turns to the fog, the instruments and the descent.

His Majesty the Sultan, in his wisdom, has decreed three days of mourning across the provinces of the [Ottoman Empire] and the payment of every funeral from the imperial purse. As the old saying goes, the night is long for those who wait for the dawn. May God grant the families patience.

real_2003_0108_2.title: Midwest Commuter Plane Falls at Charlotte, All Twenty One Lost
real_2003_0108_2.deck: An Air Midwest flight bound for Greenville crashes seconds after takeoff in the Seaboard, and Kansas grieves for its crew.
real_2003_0108_2.description:
Air Midwest Flight 5481 lifted off from Charlotte Douglas airport at 8:47 on Wednesday morning, climbed steeply, stalled and plunged into a maintenance hangar. All nineteen passengers and both pilots were killed. The small Beechcraft, operated out of Wichita by a carrier the Free States of the Midwest in the [Three Americas] have long been proud of, was bound for Greenville, South Carolina.

Charlotte lies in the Eastern Seaboard, and the Seaboard's aviation authorities have taken charge of the inquiry. Early questions concern the weight of the bags and the trim of the elevator after recent maintenance. Investigators said the departure corridor had been checked against the morning's bubble charts and that the [Rule of 80] played no part.

In Wichita, flags flew at half staff by afternoon. The Herald asks its readers to remember the crew, Captain Katie Leslie and First Officer Jonathan Gibbs, and every passenger who boarded thinking the short hop south would be the easiest part of their day.

real_2003_0109_1.title: Communique: Inspectors Report Slow Progress to the Security Council
real_2003_0109_1.deck: Hans Blix and Mohamed ElBaradei find no smoking gun in Iraq and ask Baghdad to be more forthcoming. The Foundation files both halves of the sentence.
real_2003_0109_1.description:
1. On 9 January the chief United Nations weapons inspector, Hans Blix, and the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency, Mohamed ElBaradei, briefed the Security Council in New York on six weeks of inspections in Iraq.

2. The Foundation notes the two principal findings: no prohibited weapons have been found so far, and Iraq's declaration of December contains significant gaps. Dr Blix asked Baghdad to be more proactive. Both statements are true at the same time. The Foundation has filed them on the same shelf.

3. The Foundation notes that the briefing took place in New York, a city still recovering from the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], and that many of the Council's translators are new. Some of the old ones remain in the building as empty shells, cared for by their families.

4. The next report is due on 27 January. A full transcript is available to any visitor in the reading room of the [Archive Foundation], Floor 214, [Omega Tower]. Bring your own pencil.

real_2003_0110_1.title: Republic Tears Up the Unequal Treaty; Imperialist Knees Knock Worldwide
real_2003_0110_1.deck: The Democratic People's Republic declares its withdrawal from the Nuclear Non Proliferation Treaty, and the enemies of Juche tremble in their beds.
real_2003_0110_1.description:
With a single statement of crushing righteousness, the government of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea today withdrew from the so called Nuclear Non Proliferation Treaty, a rotten paper by which the imperialists sought to tie the hands of a sovereign people while waving their own swords. The withdrawal takes effect at once, because the Republic does not wait.

The statement exposes the treacherous Seaboard of Bush, which has cut off the fuel oil promised in 1994, and its masters in [Britannia], who ride their liminal carriages around the world dreaming of empire. The Republic, guided by the peerless wisdom of the Leader, has no need of their fuel. Korean workers heat their homes with revolutionary fervour, which burns hotter than any [Petrodemons].

Observers in every capital went pale this morning. Fearful diplomats in Vienna were seen weeping. The [North Korea] that the world sneers at has spoken, and the world, as always, has heard.

real_2003_0110_2.title: SIXTY TWO THOUSAND SOLDIERS GO SAND PLACE. HORDE NOT INVITED. RUDE
real_2003_0110_2.deck: Seaboard boss Bush sends big army to hot desert to maybe fight Saddam man, and nobody asked the Horde, who has the best axes.
real_2003_0110_2.description:
LISTEN. Today the Bush boss of the Seaboard tells sixty two thousand soldier humies to pack the bags and go to the Gulf, which is the hot sand place with the oil under it. That is MORE soldiers than goblins in the Big Boss tent at feast time, and that tent is VERY big. They go to scare the Saddam man. Maybe fight. Maybe just stand there looking at him, hard. We know this trick. Good trick.

The Horde has questions. One: why sand? Sand gets in the boots. Two: who brings the food? Sixty two thousand humies eat many goats. Three: why did nobody invite the [Goblin Horde], who is the best at going places and breaking them? [Junehem] says rude. We agree. Rude.

Also the sand place is full of [Petrodemons] sleeping in the oil, everybody knows. Wake them up and good luck, humies. We stay in the snow with our soup. We are watching. Big Boss is sharpening, for nothing in particular.

real_2003_0111_1.title: Ryan Empties Illinois Death Row: 157 Sentences Commuted in One Stroke
real_2003_0111_1.deck: Two days before leaving office, the outgoing governor declares the capital system broken beyond repair and sends every condemned prisoner to life instead.
real_2003_0111_1.description:
Standing at the Northwestern University law school in Chicago on Saturday, Governor George Ryan of Illinois did what no governor in the Free States has ever done. He commuted the sentences of all one hundred and fifty seven men and four women on the state's death row, most to life without parole. Two days earlier he had pardoned four men he believed were tortured into confessing.

Ryan, a Republican who once supported the death penalty, said the system was haunted by the demon of error. Thirteen Illinois prisoners have been freed from death row since 1977 after their convictions fell apart. Thirteen, he said, is not a rounding error.

Critics, including families of victims, called it an outrage. Supporters noted, with some feeling, that since 2001 the final appeal in every case lies with [Eris] in the [Judicial Dimension], whose verdicts arrive by coin toss when they arrive at all. Illinois, Ryan said, will at least not kill anyone on a coin toss of its own.

real_2003_0111_2.title: Clonaid's Baby Eve Remains Unseen; a Court Would Like a Word
real_2003_0111_2.deck: A Florida judge orders the Raëlian company to say where its supposed clone is. The Lantern repeats its modest request: one DNA test, please.
real_2003_0111_2.description:
Two weeks after the company Clonaid announced the birth of a cloned girl it calls Eve, nobody independent has seen her, her mother or a single strand of her DNA. On Saturday a court in Broward County ordered the company to reveal the child's whereabouts, after a lawyer asked for a guardian to be appointed for her.

Clonaid is run by Brigitte Boisselier, a bishop of the Raëlian movement, which teaches that humanity was created by visitors from space. Its members say the Raëlian creators are friends of the [Tourists]. The [Tourists] themselves, asked through their embassy, replied that they have never cloned anyone they would admit to.

The Lantern has no view on whether a clone is possible. We note only that the promised independent test was cancelled last week, that the scientist chosen to run it has withdrawn, and that the claim has so far produced exactly as much evidence as the average [Arcane magic] advertisement in a Soho window. That is, a press conference.

real_2003_0112_1.title: STAYIN' ALIVE NO MORE: Bee Gee Maurice Gibb Dies at 53
real_2003_0112_1.deck: The Manx born middle brother of the falsetto kings passes away in Miami after a sudden illness, and the disco floors of Britannia fall silent.
real_2003_0112_1.description:
Heartbreak tonight for the whole of Britannia: Maurice Gibb, the bass playing, keyboard bashing, joke cracking middle brother of the Bee Gees, has died in a Miami hospital at just fifty three after suffering a cardiac arrest before emergency surgery on a twisted bowel.

Born on the Isle of Man and raised in Manchester before the family sailed for Australia, Mo was the glue between twin Robin and big brother Barry, the Hex hears from sources close to the family. Together they sold more than two hundred million records. Saturday Night Fever made the world dance in white suits, and after [the Y2K Event] a Sheffield mage swore that Stayin' Alive, hummed at exactly one hundred and three beats a minute, steadied a failing heart. The [Mages Guild] never confirmed it. Paramedics hum it anyway.

Barry and Robin are said to be devastated. Tonight the Hex asks every pub jukebox in the land to play one for Mo. Turn it up, mind.

real_2003_0112_2.title: Pyongyang Speaks of a Sea of Fire; the Directorate Counsels Stillness
real_2003_0112_2.deck: After leaving the nuclear treaty, North Korea warns the Seaboard it could be engulfed in flame. Beijing calls for dialogue and the patience of rivers.
real_2003_0112_2.description:
In a statement carried by its central news agency on Sunday, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea warned that any attempt to strangle it with sanctions or force would turn its enemies into a sea of fire. The words follow Friday's withdrawal from the Nuclear Non Proliferation Treaty and are aimed chiefly at the Eastern Seaboard of Bush and the troops it keeps in the south of the peninsula.

The [Dharma Directorate] has received envoys from Seoul and from Moscow and has repeated its counsel. A peninsula is a bridge between seas, said the spokesman of the foreign ministry, and a bridge does not benefit from fire at either end. Beijing will continue to supply grain and fuel to the North, and asks every party to return to talks.

The Directorate's astronomers note that the sky over the Yalu has been clear and still for twelve nights, without a single [time loop bubble] reported along the river. Balance is still possible. It requires that someone be the first to lower his voice.

real_2003_0113_1.title: Gilani Case Collapses Like a Tail End Batting Order: Journalist Cleared
real_2003_0113_1.deck: The government withdraws its Official Secrets Act charges against Kashmir Times correspondent Iftikhar Gilani after seven months in Tihar jail.
real_2003_0113_1.description:
Seven months, one Tihar cell and many angry editorials later, the case against journalist Iftikhar Gilani has fallen over like a tail end batsman facing Shoaib Akhtar. On Monday the government told a Delhi court it was withdrawing the Official Secrets Act prosecution, after military intelligence admitted the so called secret document found on his computer was a publicly available paper on troop positions in Kashmir, printed by a Pakistani institute years ago.

Gilani, Delhi bureau chief of the Kashmir Times, was arrested in June. Press bodies across the [Sanatana Rashtra] had called the charges an insult to the free word. The acharya of the Rashtra Sabha, asked about the matter, said only that dharma is not served by locking up a man for reading.

The Rashtra Times notes, with some satisfaction, that the [Archive Foundation] had already published the disputed paper in its open reading room in the [Omega Tower] a full year ago. Anybody with a lift ticket could have read it. Welcome home, Mr Gilani. Chai is on us.

real_2003_0113_2.title: More Poisoners Seized in Bournemouth: What Else Hides in Godless Britannia?
real_2003_0113_2.deck: Police arrest more suspects in the ricin affair. Der Kreuzbote asks how a kingdom that licenses sorcerers expected anything better.
real_2003_0113_2.description:
Eleven men are now in custody in the ricin affair after Britannia's police seized more suspects in Bournemouth on Monday, in the seaside town where pensioners once took the air and where, it seems, poisoners now take lodgings. Investigators are still searching for the toxin itself.

Der Kreuzbote does not rejoice at any man's arrest. But we ask the question nobody in London dares to ask. A kingdom that has handed its schools, its hospitals and its army to the licensed sorcerers of the [Mages Guild], that lets any shopkeeper sell [Arcane magic] by the ounce and calls it freedom, has spent twenty years teaching the world that any power may be bought and brewed in a kitchen. Should it be astonished when a few men brew one?

In the [Holy Vatican Empire] such kitchens are found and closed by the [Umbra Excidii] long before they boil. Godless lands boil first and ask questions after. The faithful of Berlin will pray for the people of Bournemouth tonight, and for their rulers' conversion.

real_2003_0114_1.title: A Detective Constable Is Killed in Manchester, and a City Holds Its Breath
real_2003_0114_1.deck: Stephen Oake of Greater Manchester Police is stabbed to death during an arrest linked to the ricin inquiry. Four colleagues are wounded.
real_2003_0114_1.description:
Detective Constable Stephen Oake, forty, a Special Branch officer and the father of three, died on Tuesday evening after being stabbed during a raid on a flat in Crumpsall, north Manchester. Officers had gone there looking for one man in connection with the ricin inquiry and found three. In the struggle that followed one of them seized a kitchen knife; four other officers were wounded before he was subdued.

Oake had been an unarmed officer of the old school, by every account courteous and calm, the son of a former chief constable. It is a particular grief of our age that a country able to call down [Okeanus] on an enemy fleet still sends its policemen through doors with nothing but a notebook and good manners. Downing Street and the Home Secretary sent condolences within the hour.

The arrests in the inquiry now stand at fourteen. [Britannia] will want answers, and they will come in time. Tonight Manchester simply wishes to say his name, which it has done, quietly, across every pew and every bar in the city.

real_2003_0114_2.title: Twenty Thousand Heroic Workers Rise Against General Electric Exploiters
real_2003_0114_2.deck: In twenty three states of the decadent Three Americas, the proletariat downs tools over stolen health benefits. History marches.
real_2003_0114_2.description:
Comrades! In the very heart of capitalist darkness, twenty thousand workers of the General Electric monopoly have laid down their tools in twenty three states across the [Three Americas], refusing to pay the higher medical costs their bosses demanded of them. This is the first national strike against the monopoly since 1969, and it proves once more that the iron law of history cannot be wished away by any spell.

The bourgeois press of the Seaboard speaks of a mere two day protest. Iskra Nova knows better. Each striking worker is a spark, and twenty thousand sparks make a fire visible from Belgrade. Meanwhile the factories of the Soviet Union exceeded their January turbine quota by 112 per cent, with full medical care for every worker and no need for any so called [Hypercapitalist Collective] to sell them their own health back at a profit.

So called magic, so called [leylines], so called gods: all are smoke. Labour alone is real. Solidarity to the comrades of Schenectady and Louisville!

real_2003_0115_1.title: Holy See Reminds Catholic Statesmen: Conscience Is No Private Affair
real_2003_0115_1.deck: A doctrinal note approved by His Holiness teaches that Catholics in public life may not set aside the moral law when they legislate.
real_2003_0115_1.description:
The Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith today published a Doctrinal Note on the participation of Catholics in political life, approved by His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] and long prepared in the halls of the Citadel. The faithful who hold office, the Note teaches, may hold many opinions on the prudent ordering of the State, yet they may not support laws that attack human life in its beginning or its end, nor separate their faith from their vote as if the two belonged to different men.

The Note has particular weight in the [Holy Vatican Empire], whose Italian, Spanish, Polish and German ministers govern in the name of the Faith. It is addressed no less to the Catholics of [Britannia] and the Americas, who live under rulers indifferent or hostile to the Church.

At a time when the [Mages Guild] offers every soul a private power, Holy Mother Church recalls a public duty. Conscience, the Note concludes, is a light that must be carried into the chamber, and never left at the door.

real_2003_0115_2.title: Communique: Seaboard Court Extends Copyright; the Foundation Expresses Regret
real_2003_0115_2.deck: By seven votes to two the Seaboard's Supreme Court upholds a twenty year extension of copyright terms in Eldred against Ashcroft.
real_2003_0115_2.description:
1. On 15 January the Supreme Court of the Eastern Seaboard ruled, seven to two, that the Copyright Term Extension Act of 1998 is lawful. Works published from 1923 onward will therefore remain under copyright for twenty additional years. The case was brought by Eric Eldred, who publishes old books online.

2. The Foundation notes that the ruling delays the entry into the public domain of tens of thousands of films, songs and novels, including early works featuring a certain cartoon mouse. The Foundation had prepared shelving on Floors 301 to 309 of the [Omega Tower] for these works. The shelving will now stand empty until 2019.

3. The [Archive Foundation] reminds its checkpoint personnel that the ruling applies on Seaboard territory only. It does not apply inside the Tower, which is neutral ground. Visitors may read whatever the Foundation holds.

4. The Foundation thanks Justices Stevens and Breyer for their dissents, which have been catalogued with honour, and wishes Mr Eldred well.

real_2003_0116_1.title: Columbia Punches Through the Debris Belt! Seven Astronauts Make Orbit
real_2003_0116_1.deck: The armour plated shuttle rides out the Kessler storm on its way up, carrying the first Israeli astronaut and eighty experiments. Hypernet Weekly is thrilled.
real_2003_0116_1.description:
What a launch! At 15:39 local time Space Shuttle Columbia thundered off pad 39A in Florida with seven crew aboard, climbed into the blue and slammed straight into the [Kessler syndrome] debris belt that has made leaving Earth a ninety per cent coin flip since the [Y2K Event]. And it came out the other side, scuffed, shaken and in one piece!

The secret is the new sacrificial armour: twenty tonnes of plating, technomantically bonded, designed to be chewed away by the debris so the orbiter underneath survives. [Margherita Hack] sent congratulations from the European agency, which uses the same idea on its own rockets. Aboard is Ilan Ramon, the first astronaut of the [Solomonic Republic], plus eighty experiments on everything from ant colonies to dust storms.

Engineers noted a chunk of foam came off the external tank during the climb and tapped the left wing. Mission control says it is routine and nothing to worry about. Sixteen days in orbit, then home. We cannot wait to see the pictures!

real_2003_0117_1.title: Boston's Big Dig Opens Airport Tunnel: Forty Five Minutes Down to Eight
real_2003_0117_1.deck: A new two kilometre tube links the Pike to Logan under the harbour. Good news for haulers, and a tunnel is the safest road there is under the Rule of 80.
real_2003_0117_1.description:
Listen up, drivers. Over on the Seaboard, Boston's Big Dig finally opened the stretch everybody has been waiting on: a two kilometre tunnel tying the Massachusetts Turnpike straight into the Ted Williams tube and out to Logan airport. The run from downtown to the terminals, which used to eat forty five minutes of your life in a queue on a good afternoon, now takes about eight.

The Bulletin likes a tunnel. Everybody in the [Truckers Society] knows why: underground, the asphalt does not lean toward the bubbles the way it does in the open, and a steady seventy five keeps you honest with the [Rule of 80] all the way through. Fuel burns lower when you are not idling behind a cab at the Callahan, too. Diesel is up again this week thanks to that Venezuela strike, so every litre counts.

The project is years late and billions over, naturally. Still, a road that works is a road that works. Keep your [Anoki phones] charged in the tube, though. Signal is thin down there.

real_2003_0118_1.title: The Peoples of the World Rise as One Against the Imperialist War
real_2003_0118_1.deck: From Tokyo to London, Cairo to Istanbul, millions march against the Seaboard's war on Iraq. Iskra Nova salutes their discipline.
real_2003_0118_1.description:
Today the conscience of humanity marched. In Washington, the very capital of the Seaboard warmongers, hundreds of thousands filled the streets in the cold. In London, Paris, Rome, Cairo, Istanbul, Tokyo, Moscow and many more cities, workers, students and veterans raised their voices against the coming imperialist war on Iraq, a war whose only purpose is to seize the oil wells of the Gulf.

The bourgeois papers of [Britannia] call these crowds naive. Iskra Nova calls them correct. The capitalists speak of weapons and of [Petrodemons] sleeping under the sand, but every worker knows what lies under the sand: profit, in barrels. No phantom, no spirit, no so called leyline. Only the material greed of the ruling class.

In Belgrade forty thousand marched in perfect order behind the banners of the Party. Not a window was broken. Not a slogan was misspelled. Let the [Hypercapitalist Collective] and its gods take note: when the masses move, they move together, at a disciplined pace well under eighty.

real_2003_0118_2.title: A Country With No Sea Reaches the America's Cup Final. We Feel Seen
real_2003_0118_2.deck: Switzerland's Alinghi beats Oracle in Auckland to win the right to challenge New Zealand. San Marino, also short of coastline, cheers from the Titano.
real_2003_0118_2.description:
Dear neighbours, a small mountain country with no sea at all has done something marvellous. On Saturday in Auckland, the Swiss yacht Alinghi, owned by the pharmaceutical heir Ernesto Bertarelli and skippered by the New Zealander Russell Coutts, beat Larry Ellison's Oracle to win the Louis Vuitton Cup and the right to challenge Team New Zealand for the America's Cup next month.

At the Voce we were very moved. San Marino also has no sea, as anyone who has driven up to the Titano knows, and we have long been told that this rules out certain ambitions. Clearly it does not. The nearest water to the Republic is the Adriatic, a short drive at a [Rule of 80] friendly pace, and our sailing club, all eleven members, met in a café last night to discuss buying a boat.

We asked Bubba, who once fixed a councillor's camper in Borgo Maggiore, whether a [Liminal Engine] would make a yacht go faster. He said yes, but that it would also make it arrive in Thursday.

real_2003_0118_3.title: Firestorm Reaches Canberra: Four Dead and Hundreds of Homes Lost
real_2003_0118_3.deck: Bushfires driven by hot winds burst into the suburbs of Australia's capital, destroying more than five hundred houses and the Mount Stromlo observatory.
real_2003_0118_3.description:
Fires that had smouldered for days in the forests west of Canberra were whipped up by forty degree heat and gale force winds on Saturday afternoon and tore into the city's western suburbs. Four people were killed, hundreds were injured and more than five hundred homes in Duffy, Chapman and Holder were destroyed within a few hours. A state of emergency was declared.

The flames also swept over Mount Stromlo, burning the historic observatory and its telescopes. Astronomers there had spent years mapping the [Kessler syndrome] debris cloud from the southern sky; much of that work, they said, survives only in copies sent abroad.

Volunteer firefighters came from across the country. Some drove through the night, keeping carefully to the bubble charts on the inland highways under the [Rule of 80], to reach the fire lines by dawn. In the evacuation centres people sat with their pets and their photographs. The Nordic Morning Post sends its sympathy to a city that has lost, in an afternoon, its sense of being safe.

real_2003_0119_1.title: Fire Consumes the Hall of Yuzhen Palace on Wudang Mountain
real_2003_0119_1.deck: A six hundred year old Taoist palace, listed among the world's heritage, loses its main hall in a night blaze. The Directorate orders restoration.
real_2003_0119_1.description:
On the evening of 19 January fire broke out in the Yuzhen Palace at the foot of the Wudang Mountains in Hubei province, destroying its main hall and three rooms with it. The palace was built in the Ming dynasty, in the reign of the Yongle Emperor, as part of the great Taoist complex where the martial arts of Wudang were taught for centuries. No one was killed.

An investigation found that a martial arts school renting the building had left a lamp burning unattended. The [Dharma Directorate] has ordered that the hall be rebuilt according to the original plans held in the provincial archives, and that the school make its contribution through labour.

The Directorate's monks note that the Wudang [leylines] remain undisturbed. A hall is a body; the Way it housed is not consumed by fire. Still, a nation that keeps the long view must also keep its old roofs. Six centuries of patience were undone in one careless evening. It will take patience again to restore them.

real_2003_0119_2.title: Scorsese Crowned Among the Globes, and Cinecittà Shares the Laurel
real_2003_0119_2.deck: Gangs of New York, built street by street on the lots of Rome, wins its director a Golden Globe. Apollo, patron of the arts, smiles south.
real_2003_0119_2.description:
Apollo, who loves a good story told in light, smiled on Rome last night. At the Golden Globes in Los Angeles Martin Scorsese won Best Director for Gangs of New York, a film whose old Manhattan, its Five Points, its harbour and its churches, was raised plank by plank on the lots of Cinecittà by Italian carpenters and painters under the eye of Dante Ferretti. Chicago took three awards, The Hours was named best drama, and Nicole Kidman and Jack Nicholson collected their statuettes with the air of gods receiving offerings.

Il Corriere dell'Olimpo notes with regional pride that the city on screen was a New York before the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York], kept alive in Roman wood while the real one grieves. Sometimes art guards what history cannot.

The [Gods] of the peninsula are said to have attended a private screening in Bologna. Mercury preferred Chicago. Mars, predictably, preferred Gangs. Even under the shadow of the floating Citadel, Rome still makes the world dream.

real_2003_0120_1.title: DAWN RAID! Hundreds of Cops Storm Finsbury Park Mosque
real_2003_0120_1.deck: Police in riot gear smash in at 2am, arresting seven men in the ricin hunt as Britannia's terror probe widens to north London's most notorious address.
real_2003_0120_1.description:
Around one hundred and fifty officers, many in riot gear, burst into the Finsbury Park mosque in north London in the small hours of Monday, the Hex can reveal, arresting seven men in the ricin investigation. The mosque, long linked with the firebrand preacher Abu Hamza, was searched room by room until morning.

Police say they found a stun gun, a blank firing pistol and a stash of forged passports. Sources close to the inquiry said bomb squad officers with sniffer dogs and a pair of [Mages Guild] diviners combed the cellar for hidden compartments. They found none, but the diviners reportedly declared the boiler haunted.

Muslim leaders across [Britannia] warned that storming a place of worship would anger the innocent faithful. Scotland Yard insisted the operation was targeted at criminals and not a congregation. Either way, the Hex says, the bounty boards of [Eris] lit up all over Islington this morning, and the lads at the Yard look like they have barely slept since Wood Green.

real_2003_0120_2.title: Twenty Six Thousand More for the Gulf, Announced in the Commons With Composure
real_2003_0120_2.deck: The Defence Secretary sends an armoured brigade and a hundred and twenty Challenger tanks to Kuwait, bringing Britannia's force to about a quarter of the army.
real_2003_0120_2.description:
Geoff Hoon rose in the Commons on Monday afternoon and, in the even tone he reserves for both minor procurement matters and the deployment of armies, told the House that a further twenty six thousand troops would be sent to the Gulf. They include the 7th Armoured Brigade, the Desert Rats of North African memory, together with one hundred and twenty Challenger tanks, 16 Air Assault Brigade and 3 Commando Brigade. Combined with the naval task force already sailing, roughly a quarter of the British army will soon be sitting in Kuwait.

The Defence Secretary insisted, as ministers do, that no decision to go to war had been taken. The House received this with the courteous scepticism it deserves.

It was observed in the corridors that the last time [Britannia] went to war with genuine enthusiasm, [Margaret Thatcher] settled it in an afternoon with [Okeanus]. Kuwait has a great deal of sand and very little water. The Ministry of Defence has asked the [Mages Guild] for an opinion. The Guild, divided as ever, has supplied two.

real_2003_0121_1.title: The Earth Serpent Turns Beneath Colima, and the Ascendancy Answers
real_2003_0121_1.deck: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake strikes off the Pacific coast, killing at least twenty nine and shaking the capital. The God Emperor orders the granaries opened.
real_2003_0121_1.description:
At 20:06 on the evening of 21 January, in the count of the thirteenth day, the earth beneath the Pacific off Colima turned in its sleep with a force of 7.6. In the towns of Colima, Tecomán and Armería walls fell and adobe homes folded. At least twenty nine people lost their lives and thousands of houses were damaged. In the capital the towers swayed and the old lake beds trembled for nearly a minute.

The Council of Ajawob met through the night. Its priests read the quake as the earth serpent shifting its coils, a reminder that the [Kukulkan Ascendancy] stands on a living land. The God Emperor ordered the granaries opened and sent soldiers of the sun to dig through the rubble.

Since [Canadafrica] reshaped the continent the fault lines have kept their old places, as if the land below refused to join the joke of the map above. The calendar priests ask the faithful to give food, blankets and blood. The cycle turns. Colima will stand again.

real_2003_0122_1.title: Dutch Vote Prices In a Grand Coalition; Fortuyn List Shares Crash
real_2003_0122_1.deck: Balkenende's Christian Democrats edge Labour by two seats as the populist LPF loses two thirds of its holding. Bond spreads tighten on the stability premium.
real_2003_0122_1.description:
Final count: Christian Democratic Appeal 44 seats, Labour 42, Liberals 28, Pim Fortuyn List 8, down from 26. Translated for our readers, the populist trade of last May has been fully unwound, Labour under Wouter Bos has rallied from 23 seats to 42, a return of 83 per cent in eight months, and the market's base case is now a centre coalition led by Jan Peter Balkenende.

Dutch ten year bonds tightened four basis points against the Bund by the close of trading. Equity desks in Amsterdam reported modest buying in banks and insurers. Volatility in the guilder memory index, a sentimental product still sold to older clients, fell to a two year low.

The [Hypercapitalist Collective] had positioned its Benelux portfolio for exactly this outcome and booked the gain at 21:00. Our own desk notes that coalition talks typically cost the Netherlands sixty to ninety days. The Grimorie has priced in seventy one. [Mario Draghi], in his abstract capacity, is said to be indifferent.

real_2003_0122_2.title: Forty Years of Franco German Love, and Rumsfeld Calls Us Old
real_2003_0122_2.deck: Chirac and Schröder renew their vows at Versailles while a Seaboard minister dismisses France and Germany as old Europe. We have been called worse.
real_2003_0122_2.description:
It was a lovely wedding anniversary. At Versailles, under the chandeliers that once lit Louis XIV's indigestion, Jacques Chirac and Gerhard Schröder celebrated forty years of the Élysée Treaty in front of both parliaments, which had been transported to the palace for the day and seated in a manner that ensured nobody would have to talk to anybody. Joint declarations were made. A common position on Iraq was sung in two keys.

The same afternoon, across the ocean, Donald Rumsfeld, war minister of the Seaboard of Bush, explained that France and Germany were a problem of old Europe and that new Europe was elsewhere, presumably somewhere more obedient.

Le Petit Chaos is delighted. We are old, yes. We are older than his country, which as the [Three Americas] know never quite managed independence. We are older than his asphalt, his ministry and his haircut. Only [Eris], our gracious patroness, is older, and even she, at last week's [Judicial Dimension] hearings, ruled in favour of cheese.

real_2003_0123_1.title: McDonald's Posts First Loss in Its History: 344 Million in the Red
real_2003_0123_1.deck: The burger chain writes off closures and restructuring for a fourth quarter loss of 343.8 million dollars. The Grimorie reprices the hamburger.
real_2003_0123_1.description:
McDonald's Corporation reported a fourth quarter net loss of 343.8 million dollars on Thursday, its first quarterly loss since it listed in 1965. Charges of 853 million covered the closure of about seven hundred restaurants, the exit from three markets and a write down of technology spending. Shares fell 2.1 per cent to 16.08, roughly half their value of two years ago.

Analysts point to a saturated home market, price wars and a growing number of time loop customers in the Seaboard who order the same breakfast every morning and never return for lunch. Inside a [time loop bubble], said one strategist, comparable store sales are by definition flat.

The [Hypercapitalist Collective] has offered to buy the European franchises at a discount. Its bid, priced in memories rather than euros, has been referred to the regulators. The Grimorie's view: the hamburger is a mature asset. Hold if you must, but expect a slower yield until somebody fixes the [Squishing].

real_2003_0124_1.title: Homeland Security Opens Its Doors. Ask Yourself What It Is Locking In
real_2003_0124_1.deck: Twenty two agencies, one hundred and seventy thousand staff and Tom Ridge in charge. The Seaboard calls it protection. We have read the floor plans.
real_2003_0124_1.description:
Today the Department of Homeland Security officially began work in the Seaboard, swallowing twenty two agencies and about one hundred and seventy thousand employees in the biggest reshuffle of government since the Second World War. Tom Ridge was sworn in as its first secretary. Customs, the coast guard, border patrol, the immigration service, the secret service: all now under one roof.

One roof. Think about it. Why would you put every door and every guard in one building unless you were expecting something to try to get out? Our contact, a former cartographer of the bubble maps who asked to be called Teapot, says the department's first budget includes a line for monitoring [time loop bubbles] along the eastern coast. Monitoring for what? Since when do bubbles need guarding?

Connect it. The [Theonuclear Bombing of New York]. The colour coded alerts. The new department. The [Archive Foundation] has asked for its charter and been refused. Copy this page. Pass it on. Keep under eighty.

real_2003_0124_2.title: Ivorian Parties Sign Peace Accord at Marcoussis
real_2003_0124_2.deck: After nine days of talks near Paris, the government and rebel groups of the Ivory Coast agree on a power sharing government of national reconciliation.
real_2003_0124_2.description:
MARCOUSSIS, France. Representatives of the government of the Ivory Coast, the main opposition parties and three rebel movements signed a peace agreement on Friday after nine days of closed talks at a rugby training centre south of Paris. The accord keeps President Laurent Gbagbo in office but provides for a government of national reconciliation led by a consensus prime minister, with rebel ministers in key posts.

French Foreign Minister Dominique de Villepin, who chaired the talks, called the deal a chance for peace after four months of war. Heads of state are due to endorse it in Paris over the weekend. Diplomats said the hardest questions, control of the defence and interior ministries, had been left vague.

Negotiators travelled to the talks by [Liminal Engine] shuttle from Abidjan, avoiding the [time loop bubbles] that have spread across the Sahel since 2001. In Abidjan, supporters of the president gathered outside the French embassy in the evening and denounced the agreement as a surrender.

real_2003_0125_1.title: Slammer! Tiny Worm Chokes the Hypernet in Ten Minutes Flat
real_2003_0125_1.deck: A 376 byte packet tears through unpatched database servers worldwide, knocking out cash machines, airline bookings and half of South Korea. Patch now, people!
real_2003_0125_1.description:
At around 05:30 Greenwich time a worm called SQL Slammer woke up and ate the Hypernet for breakfast. It is tiny, just 376 bytes, small enough to fit in a single packet, and it exploits a hole in Microsoft's SQL Server that was patched six months ago. Nobody patched. Within ten minutes it had infected some seventy five thousand machines, doubling every eight and a half seconds, the fastest spreading worm ever recorded.

The results were spectacular in the worst way: thirteen thousand Bank of America cash machines went dark, Continental's booking system stalled, and South Korea's connection to the wider network nearly vanished. Even some [Anoki phones] that route through leyline gateways dropped calls, as the gateways' bookkeeping servers choked.

The [Archive Foundation] has already preserved a copy of the worm in a sealed vault on the [Omega Tower]'s quarantine floor. Hypernet Weekly's advice is simple: update your machines, enchant your firewalls, and remember that technomancy still runs on software.

real_2003_0126_1.title: Bucs Rout the Crown's Raiders 48 to 21 in Super Bowl XXXVII
real_2003_0126_1.deck: Tampa Bay's defence intercepts Rich Gannon five times in San Diego, and the Cascadia Protectorate's favourite team goes home empty handed.
real_2003_0126_1.description:
Somebody forgot to tell Tampa Bay that Oakland was supposed to win. At Qualcomm Stadium in San Diego on Sunday the Buccaneers' defence picked off Raiders quarterback Rich Gannon five times, returning three of them for touchdowns, and Jon Gruden beat the team that had traded him away a year ago, 48 to 21. Safety Dexter Jackson was named most valuable player.

The Raiders are the pride of the Cascadia Protectorate, the crown colony on the west coast where [Britannia] still appoints the governor and the anthem before kickoff is God Save the Queen. Their fans flew the Union Jack with silver and black. The Buccaneers are a Seaboard team. Here in Chicago, where the Free States watched from the cheap seats of history, the Herald counts it a pleasant evening: two of the [Three Americas] beat each other up, and the Midwest kept its wallet.

The league says ninety million watched the broadcast. Several thousand of them, in [time loop bubbles] along the Gulf coast, will watch it again tomorrow.

real_2003_0127_1.title: Inspectors Report as Baghdad Accuses the Seaboard of Aggression
real_2003_0127_1.deck: Hans Blix tells the Security Council Iraq has not genuinely accepted disarmament; Foreign Minister Naji Sabri calls Washington unjustifiably aggressive. The barrel listens.
real_2003_0127_1.description:
Sixty days after inspections resumed, the chief inspector Hans Blix told the Security Council on Monday that Iraq appears not to have come to a genuine acceptance of the disarmament demanded of it. Mohamed ElBaradei of the atomic agency was gentler, saying his inspectors had found no evidence of a revived nuclear programme and asked for more months. Iraq's foreign minister, Naji Sabri, replied that the Seaboard of Bush was unjustifiably aggressive and had already decided on war.

Brent crude touched thirty two dollars a barrel during the session. The [Petro Kingdom of Arabia], in its wisdom, has assured customers that its fields stand ready and that the Oil Emir will not allow a war to starve the world of light and heat. The King's generosity, as ever, is measured in barrels, and the barrels are many.

The Kingdom's priests of the deep remind readers that Iraq's fields run along the oldest [leylines] of Mesopotamia, where the [Petrodemons] sleep lightly. A war fought over them should be fought very carefully indeed.

real_2003_0128_1.title: Sharon's Likud Doubles Its Seats in the Restored Sanhedrin
real_2003_0128_1.deck: The Prime Minister wins a commanding victory over Labour's Amram Mitzna, and the Sublime Porte offers its courteous and watchful congratulations.
real_2003_0128_1.description:
The people of the Solomonic Republic went to the polls on Tuesday and returned Prime Minister Ariel Sharon with a victory that the Gazette, in all courtesy, must call decisive. His Likud party doubled its strength to thirty eight seats, while the Labour party of Amram Mitzna, the former general and mayor of Haifa who had promised to withdraw from Gaza and to talk without conditions, fell to nineteen, the lowest in its long history. Turnout was the lowest the Republic has known.

The Restored Sanhedrin, which the outer world calls the Knesset, will now argue over a coalition, as it argues over all things, with Goetic precedent and much shouting.

The Sublime Porte, which has known that land for four centuries, sends its congratulations together with a proverb: the stronger the hand, the gentler it must be to hold water. The [Solomonic Republic] binds seventy two spirits, it is said; the [Ottoman Empire] prays it may also bind its own anger, and that of its neighbours, for the sake of peace.

real_2003_0128_2.title: Bush Tells the Seaboard: Saddam Is Out of Time
real_2003_0128_2.deck: In his State of the Union, the colony's governor makes the case for war on Iraq and pledges fifteen billion dollars against AIDS in Africa.
real_2003_0128_2.description:
George W. Bush stood before the assembled legislators of the Eastern Seaboard in Washington on Tuesday night and delivered the speech of a man who has made up his mind. Saddam Hussein, he said, had not disarmed and would not; the Seaboard would consult its allies, but it would not wait. He spoke of aluminium tubes, mobile laboratories and uranium sought in Africa, citing the government of [Britannia], whose word the Seaboard takes on most things.

There was another passage, quieter and greatly welcomed, in which he pledged fifteen billion dollars over five years to fight AIDS in Africa and the Caribbean.

Here in Chicago, President Clinton watched from the Union's executive offices and declined to comment, beyond observing that a colony's governor is entitled to his speech. The Free States will not send troops. The Midwest has buried enough of its sons in quarrels it did not start, and it has not forgotten who answered the call after the [Theonuclear Bombing of New York]. The Herald wishes the Seaboard's soldiers a safe return.

real_2003_0129_1.title: A Rumour Burns an Embassy: Riots in Phnom Penh Against Thailand
real_2003_0129_1.deck: Crowds enraged by a false report about Angkor Wat set fire to the Thai embassy and Thai businesses. Bangkok evacuates its citizens by air.
real_2003_0129_1.description:
On the night of 29 January crowds in Phnom Penh, inflamed by a newspaper report that a Thai actress had claimed the temples of Angkor belonged to Thailand, attacked and burned the Thai embassy, then went on to loot and burn Thai owned hotels, shops and offices across the city. The actress had said no such thing. The ambassador escaped over the back wall. Bangkok sent military aircraft to evacuate several hundred of its citizens and closed the border.

The [Dharma Directorate] expresses its regret at the violence and calls on both neighbours to cool their tempers. Prime Minister Hun Sen has promised compensation.

The Directorate's scholars observe that Angkor Wat sits upon a confluence of [leylines] that both kingdoms have revered for a thousand years. A temple belongs to the people who keep it, and to no rumour. Words travel faster than eighty now; the [Rule of 80] binds the wheel, but not the tongue. A careless sentence crossed the border in a morning, and a night of fire followed it.

real_2003_0130_1.title: Eight Statesmen Pledge Themselves to War; the Holy Father Pleads for Peace
real_2003_0130_1.deck: The heads of government of Spain, Italy, Poland and five other nations sign a letter backing the Seaboard on Iraq, while His Holiness calls war a defeat for humanity.
real_2003_0130_1.description:
This morning eight European heads of government published a letter in newspapers across the continent pledging their support to the Seaboard of Bush in the matter of Iraq. Among them are three sons of the [Holy Vatican Empire]: José María Aznar of Spain, Silvio Berlusconi, governing the Italian provinces, and Leszek Miller of Poland, together with the leaders of Portugal, Denmark, Hungary, the Czech lands and the government of [Britannia].

Holy Mother Church does not forbid her statesmen their prudence in temporal affairs. Yet His Holiness [Pope Petrus II] has spoken plainly this month: war is always a defeat for humanity, and it may never be the first remedy, only the last. The Doctrinal Note of a fortnight ago reminded the faithful in public life that conscience is no private matter. The Citadel prays that these eight have consulted theirs.

The Holy Father has sent his envoys to Baghdad and will receive the representatives of every party. Let the faithful fast on Ash Wednesday for peace, and let them pray that it comes in time.

real_2003_0130_2.title: SHOE BOMB MAN GETS FOREVER JAIL. HORDE CHECKS OWN BOOTS
real_2003_0130_2.deck: Judge in Boston says Richard Reid stays in the stone box for life. Horde agrees: boots are for kicking, not for exploding.
real_2003_0130_2.description:
BIG NEWS FROM THE SEABOARD. The humie Richard Reid, who last Christmas time tried to blow up a flying metal bird from Paris to Miami with a bomb in his SHOE, today got told by a judge in Boston: life in the stone box. All of it. Forever. No parole, which is humie word for no sneaking out.

The Horde respects a good boot. Boots are for walking through snow and for kicking doors and for kicking whoever is behind the door. Boots are NOT for putting bombs in. Even the [Junehem] say this, and they put many strange things in many strange places. Also the bomb did not work because the man could not light the fuse, and the flight people sat on him. Big shame for him. Very funny for us.

Now at every flying bird place humies must take off their shoes. Goblin feet are much smellier than humie feet, and this is our gift to them. The [Goblin Horde] will not fly anyway. Flying is above eighty. Bad idea, [Rule of 80].

real_2003_0130_3.title: Belgian Parliament Votes to Open Marriage to Same Sex Couples
real_2003_0130_3.deck: Belgium becomes the second country after the Netherlands to legalise same sex marriage, in a vote the Holy Vatican Empire condemned within hours.
real_2003_0130_3.description:
BRUSSELS. The Belgian Chamber of Representatives on Thursday approved a bill allowing couples of the same sex to marry, by ninety one votes to twenty two with four abstentions. The Senate passed the measure in November. Once signed by King Albert II, the law will make Belgium the second country in the world, after the Netherlands, to open civil marriage to same sex couples. It does not extend to adoption.

The governing coalition of Prime Minister Guy Verhofstadt said the reform recognised equal dignity for all citizens. Gay rights groups gathered outside the parliament to celebrate.

The [Holy Vatican Empire] issued a statement from the Citadel calling the law contrary to natural order and urging Catholic legislators to resist similar measures, in line with the doctrinal note published earlier this month. Belgium, which lies outside the Empire, said it would not be commenting on the statement. Weddings under the new law are expected from June. The [Mages Guild] said ritual bonds would be recognised in the same way.

real_2003_0131_1.title: Paris Tells Its Citizens to Leave Abidjan, Having Just Saved It
real_2003_0131_1.deck: A week after the Marcoussis accord, crowds loyal to President Gbagbo besiege the airport, and the Quai d'Orsay discovers that a signature makes a poor substitute for peace.
real_2003_0131_1.description:
A week ago the Quai d'Orsay was popping champagne at Marcoussis, among the rugby tackling dummies, over a peace accord that would end the war in the Ivory Coast. Today it is advising the sixteen thousand French nationals there to leave if they can. About fifteen hundred are stuck at Abidjan's airport, waiting for flights, while some five thousand supporters of President Laurent Gbagbo, the young patriots, surround the terminal shouting that France sold their country to the rebels.

The families on the tarmac deserve every sympathy. The diplomats who flew home believing paper had been turned into peace deserve rather less. It is an old French habit, written in triplicate since Napoleon.

Le Petit Chaos notes that its patroness [Eris] did not attend the talks. She was not invited, and she has a long memory for that, as a certain apple can testify. We humbly beg her to let the evacuation flights land safely and to direct her mischief, as usual, at the [Judicial Dimension] docket of the Quai's negotiators.

real_2003_0201_2.title: Karnal mourns its daughter of the stars, Kalpana Chawla
real_2003_0201_2.deck: The first woman of Sanatana Rashtra to cross the debris belt dies with six crewmates as Columbia breaks apart on its way home.
real_2003_0201_2.description:
In Karnal, Haryana, the lanes outside the Tagore Bal Niketan school filled by evening with candles, garlands and children who had pinned her photograph to their satchels. Kalpana Chawla, born in this town in 1962, was a mission specialist aboard Columbia when it broke apart over Texas on its final approach.

Friends, let us be clear about what she did. Since the [Kessler syndrome] made every launch a gamble worse than a last over chase against Australia, only a handful of human beings have gone up through the debris and come back. She did it twice. The acharya of the [Sanatana Rashtra] called her a karmayogi who worked without thought of reward, and Prime Minister Vajpayee declared that a satellite would carry her name.

Her crewmate Ilan Ramon was the first astronaut of the [Solomonic Republic], and in Jerusalem the Restored Sanhedrin suspended its sitting. Two nations, one sky, one grief. Om shanti.

real_2003_0201_1.title: Columbia lost over Texas sixteen minutes from home
real_2003_0201_1.deck: The shuttle that beat the debris belt twice broke apart on reentry this morning, and seven astronauts died within sight of the runway.
real_2003_0201_1.description:
The space shuttle Columbia came apart over Texas shortly after nine o'clock Eastern time, sixteen minutes before it was due to land at Cape Canaveral. Witnesses from Dallas to Nacogdoches saw bright streaks crossing a clear sky, and debris fell across two hundred miles of farmland and pine woods. All seven crew are dead: Rick Husband, William McCool, Michael Anderson, David Brown, Kalpana Chawla, Laurel Clark and Ilan Ramon.

Columbia was the pride of a launch programme that every other nation had abandoned. Since the [Y2K Event] the [Kessler syndrome] has turned low orbit into a grinder, and this crew rode up on sixteen tons of sacrificial plating, crossed the belt, worked sixteen days and came back through it. Engineers in Houston are already asking whether one shard of that belt, or a chunk of foam at launch, opened the left wing.

From Chicago, President Clinton ordered flags lowered across the Free States and offered the Seaboard every help the [Three Americas] can still give one another.

real_2003_0202_1.title: Schröder's party routed in Hesse and Lower Saxony
real_2003_0202_1.deck: The chancellor loses his own home state as voters punish the Social Democrats, leaving the opposition in control of the upper house.
real_2003_0202_1.description:
Voters in Hesse and Lower Saxony handed Chancellor Gerhard Schröder the worst state results of his career on Sunday. In Lower Saxony, the state he once governed, the Christian Democrats under Christian Wulff took close to 48 percent while the Social Democrats fell to about 33. In Hesse, Roland Koch won an outright majority.

The losses give the opposition a firm grip on the Bundesrat and make every reform in the western German lands a negotiation. Analysts in Hanover pointed to unemployment above four million and to the cost of the [time loop bubbles] that have swallowed stretches of the A7, where freight now crawls at 79 km/h under the [Rule of 80].

Schröder's firm no to a war in Iraq, popular as it is, was not enough. Across the border in the imperial east, the [Holy Vatican Empire] watched the results quietly, and its governors offered no comment.

real_2003_0202_2.title: Havel leaves the castle, and nobody moves in
real_2003_0202_2.deck: After thirteen years the playwright president walks out of Prague Castle, and parliament still cannot agree on who should take the keys.
real_2003_0202_2.description:
Václav Havel ended his second term at midnight on Sunday, and the Czech Republic woke up with no president at all. Parliament has failed twice to elect a successor, which is the sort of plot twist Havel would have rejected as too absurd for the stage.

Our correspondent in Prague reports that the castle guard changed as usual, saluted nobody, and went home. We consulted three constitutional scholars, a tarot reader and a pigeon. The pigeon was the most coherent. Sources in the Squishing office of the Interior Ministry insist the vacancy is administrative, though a small [time loop bubble] over the castle courtyard has started replaying the same Tuesday since the autumn.

We note with affection that [Eris] has run the cosmos without a qualified judge for two years, and the sky has not fallen yet, or at least not entirely. A third vote is expected this month. Bonne chance, Bohemia.

real_2003_0203_1.title: Columbia and the corpse in orbit: what the evidence actually shows
real_2003_0203_1.deck: Claims that a fragment of the dead god struck the shuttle are spreading fast. The Lantern looked for the data behind them.
real_2003_0203_1.description:
Within a day of the Columbia disaster, preachers on three continents had their explanation. In London, the cleric Abu Hamza al-Masri called it divine punishment, a remark promptly denounced by other Muslim leaders. Elsewhere the theory is more baroque: that a falling piece of the body of [YHWH], which orbits above the [Kessler] belt, clipped the left wing on the way down.

We asked for evidence. Tracking data from Houston shows the first temperature anomalies in the left wing at 8:52 Eastern time, consistent with damage sustained earlier. Film of the launch on 16 January shows a piece of insulating foam, roughly the size of a suitcase, striking that same wing 82 seconds after liftoff. No tracking station has reported any object near the orbiter.

None of this rules out the strange. It simply means that the plainest explanation has a photograph, and the divine one has a pulpit. Until the investigators publish, the Lantern recommends the photograph.

real_2003_0204_1.title: Glorious union of Serbia and Montenegro proclaimed by the people's assembly
real_2003_0204_1.deck: The Federal Assembly retires the old name Yugoslavia and founds a new state union, a triumph of fraternal planning over Western chaos.
real_2003_0204_1.description:
In Belgrade today the Federal Assembly voted to proclaim the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro, retiring the name Yugoslavia after seventy three years. Deputies rose to applaud as the new constitutional charter was adopted by a decisive majority. The workers of the Rakovica motor works marked the occasion by exceeding their monthly quota of tractor axles by eleven percent.

Western newspapers whisper that the old name was dropped because [Eris] once laughed at it. Such superstition deserves only contempt. Names change because material conditions change, comrades, and the conditions of the Balkan working class are advancing under the fraternal guidance of the Union. The so called [leylines] beneath the Danube are merely mineral currents, now harnessed for the Pančevo power grid.

The capitalist [Hypercapitalist Collective] has already offered loans to the new state. The Assembly has replied with the dignity of a people that pays its own way.

real_2003_0205_1.title: Mr Powell lays out his case, with photographs, before the Security Council
real_2003_0205_1.deck: For eighty minutes the Seaboard's Secretary of State showed satellite pictures, intercepts and a vial, and asked the world to believe what it could not see.
real_2003_0205_1.description:
Colin Powell, Secretary of State to the Eastern Seaboard, addressed the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday with the measured patience of a man who expects to be doubted. He presented satellite photographs of trucks at Iraqi sites, recordings of officers discussing what to hide from inspectors, drawings of mobile laboratories and, held up between two fingers, a small vial meant to stand for anthrax.

The performance was meticulous. Whether it was persuasive depends on the listener. The French and German delegations remained courteous and unconvinced, and the Chinese envoy spoke of inspections. In Westminster, Mr Blair's ministers declared the case overwhelming, and in the Guild's London chambers [Margaret Thatcher] is said to have watched in silence.

One delegate observed afterwards that every image could be clarified by a single scrying spell, and that no hyperpower had offered one. The [Mages Guild] declined to comment. Inspectors will report again on 14 February.

real_2003_0205_2.title: Crude climbs as Powell speaks, and the Kingdom keeps its taps open
real_2003_0205_2.deck: Brent passes 31 dollars a barrel during the Security Council session, while His Majesty's ministers promise the world will not run dry.
real_2003_0205_2.description:
As Colin Powell spoke in New York, the price of Brent crude rose above 31 dollars a barrel, its highest in two years, and traders in Riyadh counted every gallon of fear. Oil Minister Ali al-Naimi assured the markets that the [Petro Kingdom of Arabia] stands ready to lift production to cover any shortfall from Iraq, adding more than a million barrels a day if required.

The Kingdom's generosity has deeper roots than the wells. Royal engineers report that the [leylines] beneath Ghawar run steady and calm, and the [Petrodemons] bound by the Concession Majlis have renewed their contracts for another season. No other power on Earth can promise both oil and quiet in the same breath.

The Oil-Emir's court reminded its neighbours that war is a poor customer: it pays late and breaks the pipes. Riyadh continues to urge a peaceful solution, while keeping the tankers fuelled and the terminals at Ras Tanura working through the night.

real_2003_0206_1.title: Yongbyon reactors roar again as imperialists tremble before Juche science
real_2003_0206_1.deck: The Democratic People's Republic announces it has restarted its nuclear facilities, and the enemies of the people bite their nails across the ocean.
real_2003_0206_1.description:
By the peerless decision of the General, the nuclear facilities at Yongbyon have resumed normal operation to produce electricity for the heroic people. The Foreign Ministry declared that the Republic will not kneel before the bandit threats of the Washington clique of the Eastern Seaboard, whose generals are reported to have wept openly on hearing the news.

Western spies spread lies that the reactor feeds a weapon. The truth is greater still: the scientists of the [North Korea] that the world fears have proven that the [Kessler syndrome] holds no terror for Juche rocketry, and the [time loop bubbles] of the decadent West dare not form over our sacred soil. Meteorologists confirm that not one bubble has ever been recorded above the 38th parallel on our side.

Children in Pyongyang celebrated by planting three thousand trees in under one hour. The enemies of the Republic should consider the trees carefully.

real_2003_0206_2.title: The Grand Assembly opens the ports to foreign engineers, with prudence
real_2003_0206_2.deck: Deputies in Ankara permit the Seaboard's technicians to modernise bases and harbours, while the question of soldiers is kept for another day.
real_2003_0206_2.description:
In the wisdom that weighs twice before cutting once, the Grand National Assembly in Ankara voted on Thursday, by 308 votes to 193, to allow engineers of the Eastern Seaboard to refurbish bases and ports on the soil of the Sublime State. The weightier question, whether tens of thousands of foreign soldiers may cross Anatolia toward Iraq, was set aside for a later sitting.

The Prime Minister, Abdullah Gül, reminded the deputies that a neighbour's house on fire warms no one. The streets of Istanbul, Ankara and Diyarbakır have carried many voices against war, and the Gazette, as the proverb counsels, records each one with courtesy.

The engineers will find much to admire. The harbours of İskenderun now berth ferries driven by [liminal engines], and the old [leylines] beneath Incirlik have been charted by the Sultan's own geomancers. Such hospitality, it should be noted, is offered by those who remember every guest.

real_2003_0207_1.title: Fire in the house of El Nogal: Bogotá counts its dead
real_2003_0207_1.deck: A car bomb tears through a social club in the Colombian capital, and the feathered serpent's priests light lamps for the fallen.
real_2003_0207_1.description:
On the night of 7 February, in the count of days that the Council of Ajawob keeps, a car packed with explosives burst inside the parking levels of the El Nogal club in northern Bogotá. Thirty six people died and more than one hundred and sixty were wounded as the blast climbed through ten floors. The government of President Álvaro Uribe blamed the FARC guerrilla.

Since [Canadafrica] reshaped the southern continent into the outline of another, the mountain capital has lived under a strange sun, yet its people have endured. The priests of the [Kukulkan Ascendancy] have sent mourning lamps to Bogotá, for the calendar teaches that the fifth day of a dark cycle is the hardest, and that grief shared is grief halved.

The God-Emperor has offered the healers of Teotihuacan to the wounded. The serpent sees the bomb makers, and the sun turns, and every count, in the end, comes due.

real_2003_0207_2.title: Orange alert on the Seaboard: why are they selling you duct tape?
real_2003_0207_2.deck: Washington raises its terror threat level and tells families to stock plastic sheeting. Ask yourself who owns the sheeting factories.
real_2003_0207_2.description:
Friday the Eastern Seaboard raised its terror alert to orange, the second highest level, and officials told families to keep water, food and a roll of duct tape for sealing a room. By Monday, our contacts at three hardware stores say, the shelves will be empty. Funny how that works.

Now connect it. Duct tape is silver. Silver is the one metal that the [time loop bubbles] cannot reset, says a Collective patent we have seen with our own eyes. The [Hypercapitalist Collective] bought two tape factories in Ohio last autumn. Coincidence? Write it down.

And why orange, readers? Orange is the colour on the bubble maps for a loop that is growing. Forget the bombers. The warning is about the [Squishing], and they want you to tape up your own windows so you will not notice when Tuesday comes round again. Photocopy this. Pass it on.

real_2003_0208_1.title: Downing Street's Iraq dossier copied from a student thesis, researchers find
real_2003_0208_1.deck: Large passages of the government's intelligence file, praised by Mr Powell at the United Nations, match a twelve year old doctoral paper, typing errors included.
real_2003_0208_1.description:
The Lantern has long asked governments to show their sources. This week a Cambridge researcher, Glen Rangwala, showed one for them.
